title: At the Airport and on a Plane
summary: Learn easy and useful English for traveling by air. You will learn how to find your gate and talk to flight attendants.

sections.p: When you arrive at the airport, you need to find your gate. The gate is the place where you wait before you get on the plane. Look at the big screens to see your flight number and gate letter. If you cannot find it, ask airport staff for help.

ex.mean: Asking the location of your boarding gate

ex.en: My flight to Paris is at two o'clock.
ex.mean: Telling someone your flight time and destination

sections.p: Before you go to the plane, you must go to the check-in desk. Here, you give your passport and ticket to the worker. They will check your bags. They give you a boarding pass, which is a special paper you need to show before you enter the plane.

ex.en: Here is my passport and ticket.
ex.mean: Giving your travel documents to the worker

ex.en: I have one suitcase to check.
ex.mean: Telling the worker how many big bags you have

sections.p: When you are inside the plane, find your seat number. Put your small bag under the seat in front of you, or up high in the overhead locker. Flight attendants are the workers on the plane. They are there to help you and keep you safe.

ex.en: Can I have some water, please?
ex.mean: Asking a flight attendant for a drink

ex.en: Excuse me, where is seat twelve B?
ex.mean: Asking where your specific seat is located

tip: Practice these phrases out loud before your trip. Imagine you are talking to a real worker at the airport!
